assumption: LLMs trained on AI-generated content maintain original quality indefinitely
hypothesis: The Inbreeding Deterioration Hypothesis: When LLMs are iteratively trained on outputs generated by previous generations of similar models, they experience systematic quality degradation across multiple capabilities including reasoning, factual accuracy, and code generation
impact: If proven, this would establish fundamental limits on AI self-improvement and require new training methodologies
evidence: 4.5% F1 score deterioration in mixed condition by Generation 3 with 8.0 percentage point net effect vs control

assumption: All LLM capabilities degrade at the same rate during iterative training
hypothesis: Capability Asymmetry Hypothesis: Mathematical reasoning and code generation capabilities degrade faster than factual knowledge retention during iterative AI training cycles
impact: Would inform selective training strategies and early warning systems for model collapse

assumption: Quality degradation follows a linear pattern
hypothesis: Exponential Decay Hypothesis: LLM performance degradation follows an exponential decay function, with each generation losing a consistent percentage of capability rather than a fixed amount
impact: Would enable predictive modeling of when models become unusable and inform training frequency decisions

assumption: Benchmark performance changes are random and uncorrelated
hypothesis: Predictive Indicator Hypothesis: Certain benchmarks serve as early warning indicators that predict severe degradation in other capabilities before it becomes apparent
impact: Would enable development of model health monitoring systems and preventive interventions

assumption: Information content remains stable across training iterations
hypothesis: Information Entropy Reduction Hypothesis: Each generation of iterative training reduces the information entropy and diversity of model outputs, leading to increasingly homogenized responses
impact: Would provide theoretical foundation for understanding the mechanism behind model collapse
evidence: Mixed condition shows complex diversity patterns: +34.3% distinct 2-grams increase (compensatory) but -6.1% semantic similarity decline
